label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The silhouette is a plain cube in all ten views (sides.png), with no hub, spokes or rim. The brief asks for a round valve wheel, so the outline is wrong in every view.

M2.reason: The measured size is 32 x 32 x 24, with 32 across as the brief asks (sizeOff 0), which is within 15%. The size is right even though the shape is not.

M3.reason: The valve wheel's parts are missing: no hub, no spokes, no rim. The model is one solid box with no components.

M4.reason: The whole surface is uniform grey stone-like texture. The brief's red paint is absent everywhere, and the worn-to-steel rim is not there either.

M5.reason: There is no rim wear, no paint loss, and no markings. The only surface detail is a generic noise texture that does not sit where a worn valve wheel's detail would be.

M6.reason: In lineup.png the item is the grey box B, beside a rock, a sphere and a bone. No player would take a plain grey cube for a Half-Life valve wheel, so this fails the visual fidelity test.

M7.reason: A valve wheel stands upright as a disc with a front face. The box has no front, no disc orientation, and no wheel face to stand on its origin the way one would.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The model has 12 triangles, far under twice the Half-Life median of 62 for this size (124), and the closed box has no holes, inversions or floating parts.
